sources.title: USB 2.0 Specification, section 7.2.1
sources.ref: A high-power port's VBUS is 4.75 V to 5.25 V. A unit load is 0.1 A, and a high-power port supplies at least five unit loads. V is 5. Ilimit is 0.5 A, that five-unit-load ceiling: the model stays a voltage source at Ilimit and enters current limit only above it, so a load of five unit loads stays on the Thevenin line. The USB-IF drop test loads a PC USB 2.0 host at 0.5 A and still requires VBUS of at least 4.75 V.

sources.title: Series resistance, assumed
sources.ref: Rs is 0.5 ohm, assumed. It is the resistance that places a 0.5 A load on the 4.75 V floor of the cited VBUS range, and it is the cable figure used by sfab/usb-port-500ma.
